assignments.name: Group Pilgrim Bank Part 2 - Predictive
assignments.instructions:
Context and Objective:

Alan has to try to address the disagreement about online banking and should prepare a presentation to the senior management team detailing some analysis of the data available about customers. Here is case file Pilgrim_Profitability.pdf (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/files/16656881/download) Download Pilgrim_Profitability.pdf (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/files/16656881/download)and the data file PilgrimBankData.jmp (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/files/16656854/download)Download PilgrimBankData.jmp (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/files/16656854/download)

There are a few things to note about columns for Age and Income .

First, the two columns are nominal (categorical). In JMP you will be able to add these to the regression model without too much trouble because the modeling type has been changed to nominal. 

The original data does not have Age and Income data for all of the customers. JMP will automatically ignore the rows that have missing customer data.

We will ignore the District data for now and assume there is not much difference between customers in different geographic areas.

In Group Pilgrim Bank -Descriptive (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/quizzes/292364), we explored the variables and conducted some basic exploratory data analysis to understand the relationships between variables. In this assignment, we will focus on building linear regression models to understand the profitability of Online customers. 

Tasks:

Specifically, do the following analysis and comments on your results. 

Create a simple regression model (all customers) using only the 1999 data for the customer profitability and whether they use the online banking or not. Does this regression model agree with Alan’s result? Does this model support the online banking program?

Continue the analysis on profitability, create a multiple regression model with tenure as well as online banking participation. What do these results tell you about the online banking program?

Continue the analysis on profitability, create a multiple regression model using online banking participation, tenure, age and income. What does the regression results tell you about the online banking program? (No need to interpret the impact of Age and Income for this assignment)

Included in the data is information about customer profitability and whether they are online in 2000 as well as tenure, age and income (they don't really change from 1999 to 2000). Does a regression model that uses information for 2000 change your recommendation about the online banking program? 

Based on the above analysis, provide two specific recommendations on how Pilgrim Bank should proceed with the online banking product.

assignments.name: Group Store24 Analysis
assignments.instructions:
Objective:

In this project, we're going to build a model to understand the effects of Tenure on profitability. We're also going to work on how to present our findings in a business context rather than load the presentation with technical information. Here is our case file Store24__A___Managing_Employee_Retention-1.pdf (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/files/16656948). 

Part 1: Build a regression model 

In this part, our focus is on building a regression model, specifically, we will do the following:

Conduct descriptive analytics on each of the variables. Identify some key information. 

Conduct descriptive analytics on the variables pair-wise. Identify the best predictor X and identify any concern of collinearity. 

Run the best simple regression and briefly discuss the results. 

Develop the final model. Describe briefly the steps. Discuss the final model fit, interpretation of each variable coefficients. 

Part 2: Present findings

Now we have completed the analysis for Store24, we have developed many evidences about the impact of Crew tenure as well as Manager tenure on the profitability of a store controlled by other factors. We have critically evaluated and commented on these evidences. Such comments would be what we share with analysts for them to validate our analysis and technical results. The next step, is to communicate these findings to a non-technical people, colleagues from other departments or VPs or the board etc. The objective is not to stress on the analysis but to showcase findings. The language we use should be tailored to the audience. Overall, we need to communicate "what we found" but not "what we did".

Here is the dataset for store24. Store24-Exhibit3.jmp (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/files/16656801)

The following is a possible structure for the slide deck:

the situation (what) and the complication (why). Some people also like to give audience a preview (an appetizer not the main course) of the findings so that various audience can decide whether they want to stay for the duration (main course). 

logic (basic assumptions)

Findings (sensitivity). this is the main course.

Recommendations (what to do now and what can be done in the future) 

Here, I also included an additional example on how to present regression results (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/pages/an-example-of-presenting-your-findings-from-regression). it should give you some ideas what to do and what to avoid. 

What to submit:

Please submit ONE slide deck for presentation and one deck including technical details. The presentation deck should be tailored for a 20-mins presentation to non-technical audience.

announcements.title: Class 1.5 (9/2) Association of Two Categorical Variables
announcements.body:
Today in class, we continued to discuss how to describe the association between two variables. Specifically, there are three scenarios: 

For two Quantitative variables, such relationship is called correlation. We use 1) scatter plot and 2) correlation coefficient r. 

For one Categorical x variable and one Quantitative y variable, we use JMP to generate the Diamond graph (or box plot ) and do ANOVA analysis (JMP knows what to do), and observe the group means.

For TWO Categorical variables, we only observed association. Next class, we will describe it and apply it.

In addition, we continue to generalize what we observed from the sample to infer about the population. We comment on the questions: should we trust it?

Here is the course notes and recording (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/pages/annotated-notes-and-recordings) for today.

announcements.title: Class 1.2 (8/26) Describe One Variable Graphically
announcements.body:
Today in class, we discussed how to implement and interpret graphs, such as Histogram (for Quantitative) and Bar Chart (for Categorical, next class).

Histogram offers insights into the observed shape of the data, which is compared to the expected shape from the empirical rule.

If expected and observed shapes are consistent, then our numerical story checks out.

If meaningful differences are identified, we might need to identify the reasons, such as missing factors or errors.

If there is no errors, then we will interpret the skewness.

HINTS: to create the bins, we can use Excel default histogram to get a width for the bins (ex: 236 for sqft). Then we can make judgement call to decide a more appropriate bin size (ex: round up to 250 or round down to 200). 

Here is the course notes and recording (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/pages/annotated-notes-and-recordings) for today. 

Assignments after class:

Review simulation on Data Analysis Toolpak (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/pages/excel-simulation-numerical-descriptive-toolpak) and Excel Histogram (https://canvas.emory.edu/courses/165666/pages/simulation-excel-creating-histogram)
